quotes.text: Security pros consistently recommend implementing least privilege alongside a proper tiered admin model. That way help desk staff, system admins, and enterprise architects all have access scope to their actual roles instead of everyone wearing the same crown.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The danger isn't with encryption algorithms, they're solid. The problem is with how certificate templates are configured, who's allowed to request them, and what privileges those templates grant.

takeaways: A single compromised user account can escalate to domain admin through lateral movement, cached credentials and pass-the-hash if Active Directory is left on defaults.
Reducing domain admins, enforcing a tiered least-privilege model and restricting service accounts removes the most common escalation paths.
Certificate templates and hybrid sync connectors need regular audits, logging and consistent MFA and Conditional Access, or they become hidden paths into both on-premises and cloud.
hook: Active Directory still holds the keys to logins, files and email in most organizations, and attackers know it. This episode is for IT admins and security teams running on-premises or hybrid identity. It walks through the attack paths from one stolen account to domain control and the three areas to fix first: admin blast radius, PKI templates and hybrid connector hygiene.
